analysis.investment_thesis: Active Infra is a tiny, recently-listed civil construction micro-cap whose revenue inflected from ₹1 Cr to ₹90 Cr in three years and whose 2025 equity jump (₹27→₹116 Cr) reflects IPO proceeds, not organic compounding. At 26x P/E for a sub-scale, cyclical, working-capital-heavy contractor with FCF collapsing to ₹2 Cr in FY25, the price already reflects heroic assumptions with zero margin of safety.
key_strengths: Deleveraged post-IPO: borrowings down ₹109→60 Cr while equity rose to ₹116 Cr
EBITDA margin expanding (₹13→28 Cr) with ROCE at 15.5%
key_risks: FY25 OCF crashed to ₹5 Cr and FCF to ₹2 Cr despite ₹13 Cr reported profit — earnings quality deteriorating
Revenue flat/declining in FY25 (₹97→90 Cr) — the hyper-growth story is already cracking
Civil construction is cyclical, WC-intensive, and unproven through a downturn at this scale
red_flags: Classic SME/recent-IPO pattern: capital raised at peak optimism, flat top-line immediately after
Operating CF (₹5 Cr) vastly below reported PAT (₹13 Cr) in FY25
Total assets doubled to ₹220 Cr in one year — receivables/inventory build likely
analysis.detailed_analysis: Second-level thinking: the market sees "construction micro-cap with 348% 3-yr revenue CAGR and 15.5% ROCE" and pays 26x earnings. But that CAGR is an artifact of a ₹1 Cr base in 2022, and the truth is FY24→FY25 revenue actually contracted from ₹97 Cr to ₹90 Cr. Meanwhile OCF collapsed from ₹32 Cr to ₹5 Cr and investing outflows continued — a textbook working-capital-driven contractor where reported profit diverges from cash. The ₹63 Cr of financing inflow in FY25 is the IPO, which mechanically boosted book value but doesn't change the underlying economics.\n\nWhere are we in the cycle? Indian SME/micro-cap construction is firmly in the euphoria quadrant — IPOs sold at cycle peaks when optimism is highest, exactly Marks's warning. A ₹267 Cr market cap for ₹13 Cr PAT with decelerating revenue and deteriorating cash conversion offers no margin of safety; a mild sector slowdown or a single large receivable write-off could halve earnings. The downside floor is arguably book value (~₹73/share vs ₹170 price), implying 55%+ permanent loss risk in a stress scenario. Risk/reward is decidedly asymmetric to the downside. Pass.
